77052.subject: ⚔️ Anthropic had enough of Nvidia
77052.body:
----------
######                  [Collaborate with us](https://utm.genai.works/r/he2t9cz)


--------------------
View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/8776fa6e-e2d0-4aec-9648-1bed6de3a659/GenAI_Daily_Banner.jpg?t=1778687445)
Caption: 


----------

----------
**Welcome back!** Anthropic told the world it's building its own chips, which is a polite way of saying it wants out from under Nvidia. Demis Hassabis handed off the day job at Google DeepMind to go chase AGI, and Alphabet dropped about 4% while the people who built Gemini headed for the door. Microsoft told its own engineers to stop using Microsoft's coding model and use OpenAI's instead. And Ilya Sutskever, after two silent years and billions of dollars, is reportedly about to launch a model.

**In today's Generative AI Newsletter:**

* **Anthropic:** What is it building to get off Nvidia?

* **Google:** Is AGI closer than expected?

* **Microsoft:** Why pick ChatGPT over its own model?

* **Ilya:** What did two silent years buy?


----------



----------
## Anthropic is after Nvidia

View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/8648ac7b-fac8-4eb9-8e08-edb6dada1d1c/NL_-_Aug_6_1.jpg?t=1786006036)
Caption: 

Anthropic [confirmed it's hiring a team to design its own chips](https://techcrunch.com/2026/08/05/anthropic-is-hiring-an-ai-chip-design-team/), the first time it has said so out loud.

It wants to build the hardware and the models together, so Claude runs faster and cheaper on silicon designed for it. The Information reported last month that Anthropic has been scouting Samsung to build them.

The custom chips are meant to sit alongside what it already buys from AWS, Google, Nvidia and AMD rather than replace any of it. Demand for Claude keeps climbing while every lab in the business races to lock up infrastructure.

OpenAI showed off its Broadcom-built Jalapeño inference chip in June, Google has run on its own TPUs for years, and Meta builds MTIA accelerators.

Anthropic still has to buy Nvidia chips for years either way. This is about what it pays for them after that.


----------







----------

## [Stay Compliant Without Leaving Your Favorite AI Tool](https://utm.genai.works/r/6sph7e9)

Caption: 

If your team builds with Claude, Cursor, or Codex, your compliance workflow should too.

Join this live session from Vanta to see how you can manage security and compliance directly inside the AI tools you already use—saving time, reducing context switching, and keeping your team moving.

77050.subject: The New Enterprise AI Go-To-Market Playbook 📚
77050.body:
View this post on the web at https://linas.substack.com/p/enterprise-ai-gtm-playbook

👋 Hey, Linas here! Every day, I break down 3 stories shaping the future of FinTech & Artificial Intelligence - plus the money movements and trends worth tracking. First time here? 398k+ FinTech and AI leaders get this daily. Join them:
AI founders have a distribution problem disguised as a product problem. Two founders can build equally strong products, raise similar rounds, and land in opposite outcomes 18 months later, one compounding revenue while the other rots in permanent pilot purgatory, because they answered a go-to-market question they never consciously asked. A16z partner Joe Schmidt and Julian Marx named the split in a recent essay, “Lighthouse or Landgrab?”: there are two fundamentally different enterprise AI sales motions, and many founders default to the wrong one.
The diagnosis rests on two questions: how exposed is the person signing the deal, and does social proof travel in that market. Answer them correctly, and you know whether to spend the next year courting 3 Fortune 100 logos or signing 300 mid-market accounts. Answer them wrong, and you burn a funding round finding out the hard way.
That’s exactly why the rest of this guide:
Breaks down the two-question test to run before you hire your first salesperson
Explains why 95% of enterprise GenAI pilots die before production
How Sierra, Glean, Abridge, Rogo, Legora, Clay, and Cursor each picked their lane
The traps that kill both strategies, and a 7-point checklist for winning your market before an incumbent like Salesforce or ServiceNow closes the gap.
It also connects the framework to the two guides that pair with it: How to Build an AI Monopoly [ https://substack.com/redirect/da574d39-4e41-406b-9188-e0445afd629c?j=eyJ1IjoiMXN4Zm00In0.wehL2Vke0PUDz1PHD6ZKtcy1ufIoeqpblecCEEWPpqI ], on whether your market can be owned at all, and Attention Is the New Startup Infrastructure [ https://substack.com/redirect/861c6b4a-2862-4d42-bb60-e70a75e2f1ff?j=eyJ1IjoiMXN4Zm00In0.wehL2Vke0PUDz1PHD6ZKtcy1ufIoeqpblecCEEWPpqI ], on the distribution engine both motions run on.
And for the first time, the playbook ships as working software: at the end of this piece you can download lighthouse-landgrab, a Claude skill that runs the full two-question diagnostic on your company, drafts your motion plan, and audits the traps, with installation taking about 2 minutes.
Let’s dive in.
The Framework: Lighthouse vs. Landgrab...

Unsubscribe https://substack.com/redirect/2/eyJlIjoiaHR0cHM6Ly9saW5hcy5zdWJzdGFjay5jb20vYWN0aW9uL2Rpc2FibGVfZW1haWw_
